svg.title: P019 · Units sold per product
svg.desc: One row per product ID appearing on a sale line. All three sale lines survive. Lines 1 and 2 match Pen. Cup occurs only in Products and supplies no sale line. Pen has 2 + 3 = 5 units, two line IDs and two distinct order IDs (10, 11). Bag has one of each. Pen leads Bag, 5 units to 1. The output reconciles to 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 input units. First · FROM OrderDetails. The task covers products that appear on sale lines. Each detail row supplies the product ID, order ID and quantity needed to count sales. Second · LEFT JOIN Products. Use the sold ProductID to look up its catalogue name. The left join keeps a line and its quantity if that lookup fails. Its name becomes NULL. Unsold Cup contributes no line.
svg.text: One row per product ID appearing on a sale line.
Pen has two order lines. Which values produce five sold units?
A triangle marks an example to follow. Shaded columns show what to read. Double underlines mark the matching keys. SQL excerpts use … for

g.text: The task covers products that appear on sale lines. Each detail row supplies the product ID, order ID and quantity
Use the sold ProductID to look up its catalogue name. The left join keeps a line and its quantity if that lookup fails. Its
name becomes NULL. Unsold Cup contributes no line.

svg.text: All three sale lines survive. Lines 1 and 2 match Pen. Cup occurs only in Products and supplies no sale line.
OrderDetails LEFT JOIN Products ON OrderDetails.ProductID = Products.ProductID
What do units, lines and orders count?
Pen has 2 + 3 = 5 units, two line IDs and two distinct order IDs (10, 11). Bag has one of each.
How do the sales totals determine rank?
Pen leads Bag, 5 units to 1. The output reconciles to 2 + 3 + 1 = 6 input units.
ORDER BY SUM(Quantity) DESC, O.ProductID ASC
